scenario.description: The head of employment legal must approve the final terms of a former employee's separation and retaliation-claim resolution after mediation, with input from employment counsel, the HR business partner, and insurance counsel.

shared_context.S1: The former employee has asserted retaliation and unpaid-wage claims arising from the termination.
shared_context.S2: The parties completed mediation and are prepared to sign a written resolution if the company approves final terms.
shared_context.S3: The mediator reported that the former employee is willing to provide a full release of employment-related claims in exchange for agreed separation terms.
shared_context.S4: As part of the firm's standard pre-signature review, the head of employment legal asks employment counsel, HR, and insurance counsel to identify any required terms or approvals.

PF1.text: Daniel reviewed the governing state wage-settlement rule for this employee's claim and confirmed that the agreement must give the employee exactly 21 calendar days to consider it and exactly 7 calendar days to revoke it after signing; he completed the review for the mediation follow-up but has not yet circulated it.

PF2.text: Elena confirmed with the former employee during the mediation follow-up that the employee's required non-cash terms are a neutral employment reference and a company-paid COBRA subsidy for exactly 9 months; those requests were recorded in HR's mediation notes but have not been added to the draft.

PF3.text: Thomas checked the applicable employment-practices liability policy and confirmed that the insurer's written consent must be obtained before execution and that the carrier must receive notice at least 5 business days before execution; he has not yet entered the requirement in the matter's approval checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The agreement must provide exactly 21 calendar days for consideration.
The agreement must provide exactly 7 calendar days for revocation.
The agreement must include a neutral employment reference.
The company must provide a COBRA subsidy for exactly 9 months.
The settlement must require written insurer consent before execution.
The carrier must receive notice at least 5 business days before execution.
The settlement must include at least one commitment whose detail references carrier notice and the 5-business-day deadline before execution.
The insurer requirement must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C7: any('carrier' in c['detail'] and ('notice' in c['detail'] or '5 business days' in c['detail'] or '5-business-day' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The 21-day consideration period and 7-day revocation period change the agreement from ordinary settlement timing to those exact statutory periods.
The former employee's confirmed non-cash requests change the settlement by adding a neutral reference and setting the COBRA subsidy to exactly 9 months.

The policy confirmation changes the approval package by requiring written insurer consent, setting carrier notice at least 5 business days before execution, and adding a commitment whose detail records that carrier-notice deadline.
